newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse closes in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse closes in cautious trade.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse on Wednesday closed 1.42 percent higher with main stocks increasing in value with small volumes traded, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 547.69 points from 540.05 points on Tuesday, a bourse official said.
"Shareholders are cautious with the introduction of the electronic trading, they are waiting to see how things will proceed," a broker at ABN Amro Finance said.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one the leading stocks which was introduced on the continuous trading under the electronic system gained nine dirhams to close at 495 dirhams.
Samir oil refinery jumped 10 dirhams to 260 dirhams. Fertima fertilisers firm took 16 dirhams at 244 dirhams. Sonasid steel giant closed at 435 dirhams. All three were traded on the fixing.
BCM, one of Morocco's largest banks, rose 14 dirhams to close at 745 dirhams.
It showed a net profit of 615.8 million dirhams ($66 million) in 1996, up 18.82 percent over the previous year, a bank official said.
One of the eight banks listed on the Casablanca stock exchange, BCM has a market capitalisation of 9.6 billion dirhams, the second largest after the private conglomerate ONA Group.
The day's best performer was Lafarge ciment -- the result of the merger of the three cement firms Cinouca, Cadem and Lafarge Maroc last December -- soared 109 dirhams to 1091.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private group advanced by five dirhams at 695 dirhams.
Wafabank, was up four dirhams to close at 700 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 37.3 million dirhams from 24.8 million on Tuesday, a stockbroker said. ($1= 9.4 dirhams)
